title: Ayah Lens demo script Version 3
status: v0.2.1 opening-order revision; render and independent visual review pending; temporary guide narration; masjid slot reserved
opening_note: Let viewers hear the recitation, explain the population and understanding gap, then reveal the same recorded passage with its meaning. Keep the uninterrupted proof section intact.
production_notes: The opening is an edited listen/reveal replay. The review cut reserves1:00–1:30 for masjid footage; its current fill is explicitly labelled reference footage, not completed30-second masjid proof.
The review opening uses the supplied native112:1–4 excerpt. Its first eight seconds are replayed in the meaning reveal. Keep real source audio and display labels accurate.
The viewer condition matters: say “If Arabic is unfamiliar.” Do not assume that every judge is unfamiliar with Arabic or claim that all Muslims lack understanding.
The prayer scene presents a possible use. Keep its religious-permissibility disclaimer readable beside the scene and repeat it in the final video description.

The Show English meaning switch is implemented in Build 31. The wearer confirmed English disappears and returns on phone and glasses while Arabic keeps following. Capture the actual control in a separate take.

If the translation switch is unavailable, replace the 2:18–2:32 narration with: “The phone preview mirrors the selected lens window. The full passage remains available on the phone. The glasses keep a compact portion in view as the recitation continues.”
The source text is published Tanzil Arabic and Pickthall English. Spark supplies paired source boundaries; it does not author the displayed translation.
The filmed long-passage plans are cached. Voice transcription is live. Complete reference coverage is not a full-Quran accuracy result.
The population estimate comes from Pew Research Center: https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2025/06/10/islam-was-the-worlds-fastest-growing-religion-from-2010-to-2020/
Create text, diagrams and labels in post. Do not generate scripture text inside imagery. Preserve the original published wording.
Any enlarged phone preview or explanatory graphic remains labelled. Show the actual compact glasses display accurately.

Optional stretch reveal: a second person selects a prepared recitation excerpt while hands stay off the phone. Film only after successful acquisition/recovery checks. Do not call this any-verse or blind full-Quran accuracy proof.
Present Hifz as using an Arabic reference while rehearsing. Demonstrate the existing visibility switch and recitation-following behavior.

Quran teaching is a future direction requiring dedicated development and extensive evaluation with qualified teachers. The current implementation uses pretrained Muse models; no specialized teaching model has been trained or validated.
rubric_notes: Impact 30%: turn an unfamiliar-language listening experience into something the viewer can personally recognize, then establish population scale and prayer/home use.
Meta tooling 25%: connect the glasses, live speech model and Spark-assisted source pairing to the visible experience. Explain cached plans honestly.
Technical execution 20%: make within-passage movement the second reveal, followed by source preservation, actual implementation evidence and tests.
Demo 25%: use the edited opening reveal, a genuine 30-second continuous take, matched scenes and a closing return to the original image.

segments.title: Let the viewer hear before explaining
segments.visual: Warm paper opens with a clipped headline and travelling explanatory sound envelope. Play the original eight-second recitation without narration.

segments.title: Make the experience universal
segments.narration: If Arabic is unfamiliar, you just felt the gap between hearing words and following their meaning. About two billion people are Muslim, roughly one quarter of the world’s population. For many of us, that gap is part of everyday listening. What if meaning could stay with us?
segments.visual: One hundred marks arrive, twenty-five turn red, and the marks regroup into four equal groups. About 2 billion and about one quarter land beside the dated Pew source caption.
segments.overlay:

Pew Research Center · 2020 estimate, published 2025 · underlying share 25.6%

segments.title: Reveal the meaning
segments.visual: Traced rules introduce the native glasses recording and an enlarged crop from the same frames. Both source labels remain visible.

segments.title: Name the product and Meta stack
segments.narration: Meet Ayah Lens. Meta glasses, Muse Voice, and Muse Spark, working together to bring Quran recitation and its English meaning into view.
segments.visual: Original animated 3D geometry approximates the black Meta Ray-Ban Display. A changing perspective and moving light accompany staggered stack names. Label 3D illustration; the lenses contain no invented output.
segments.overlay:

segments.title: Carry one listening experience between settings
segments.narration: During Salat, Muslim prayer, it could help listeners follow the recitation. At home, it can follow a reciter playing on television. Hands free.
segments.visual: Prayer and home listening settings share travelling explanatory sound envelopes and a traced rule. The prayer disclaimer stays readable.
segments.overlay: Technology demonstration only. This does not establish religious permissibility for use during prayer.

segments.title: Prove the live experience without cuts
segments.visual: The exact 60–90-second reserved masjid block starts with a six-second placeholder. Existing phone reference then plays with its persistent replacement label and advancing slot rail.
segments.overlay:

segments.title: Reveal the difficult part hiding in plain sight
segments.narration: Now look closer. We are still inside the same passage. A long verse cannot fit on this lens. Ayah Lens follows the recitation through it, showing the relevant portion as the words continue. Nobody is turning a page.
segments.visual: An explanatory highlighted source window advances over abstract word positions. The genuine 73:20 phone source card keeps changing on the right, with no change to its wording or playback speed.
segments.overlay:
Same passage · changing portions
No manual paging

segments.title: Explain the actual AI and tracking work
segments.narration: Muse Voice converts the glasses’ audio into Arabic text. Muse Spark helps pair Arabic phrases with portions of a published English translation. It can also assist with uncertain passage matches. Our software tracks the position, validates the source boundaries, and sends the current portion to the glasses.
segments.visual: Animated data moves from glasses audio through Muse Voice transcription, local canonical matching and portion tracking, published Arabic/Pickthall source, and the lens window. Spark branches only when needed for bounded ambiguity and validated cached paired-source plans.
segments.overlay:

segments.title: Show memorization practice and listener choice
segments.narration: Hifz means memorizing the Quran. Arabic-only mode offers a reference while rehearsing. Turn English back on whenever you want to follow the meaning.
segments.visual: A labelled Hifz reference schematic gains published English meaning as an explanatory mode change. This graphic is not filmed switch proof or a tajweed grader.

segments.title: Establish the working foundation
segments.narration: The reference covers all 114 surahs. We built the glasses integration and automatic following during this hackathon. Fifty-nine tests cover matching, source preservation, and display scheduling. With further development and extensive testing, future versions could support Quran teaching.
segments.visual: The 114-surah, 6,236-reference-ayah and 59-test figures build separately. A yellow future-teaching insert states that further development and extensive testing are required.

segments.narration: The words were already there. Ayah Lens brings their meaning into view. Hear the recitation. Follow the meaning.
